pool.text: Captain William Brown of Great Britain sailed into what is now Honolulu Harbor.
Kamehameha I moved his royal court from the Island of Hawaiʻi to Waikiki.
His court relocated to what is now downtown Honolulu.
The capital was moved back to Kailua-Kona.
Kamehameha III moved the permanent capital of the Hawaiian Kingdom to Honolulu.
The independent Hawaiian Kingdom was overthrown.
The Empire of Japan attacked nearby Pearl Harbor on December 7.
Honolulu became the capital of the state of Hawaii.
The Census Bureau reported the population racial percentages for Honolulu.
Modern air travel brought 7.6 million visitors annually to the islands.
Honolulu had a 4.5% increase in average rent.
Skyline was approved by public referendum.
The Honolulu Academy of Arts and The Contemporary Museum merged.
One report found that cost of living expenses were higher.
A percentage of Honolulu households were identified as car-free.
Bikeshare Hawaii began administering the bicycle sharing program in Oʻahu.
An expansion added Biki stations toward specific local campuses and areas.
The stadium was closed.
Rick Blangiardi began serving as the county's 15th mayor.
Plans for a new stadium at the site were announced.
